title: Modeling Medea gene-drive population replacement: thresholds and release strategies
summary: Mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue, Zika, and yellow fever impose a substantial global health burden, motivating genetic control strategies that replace wild mosquito populations with disease-refractory ones. Maternal-effect dominant embryonic arrest (Medea) is a gene drive in which the offspring of a Medea-carrying mother die unless they inherit the Medea allele, producing biased inheritance capable of driving a linked refractory trait to high prevalence.
